entries.notes: Graph records must have a named consumer, authoritative source, rebuild procedure, and health state before retention; they have no independent evidence or identity write authority.
Embedding and vector-backed indices are rebuildable retrieval support, subject to capability health and authoritative-record preservation.
Current meta and ambient surfaces are feature-gated projections or selection aids, not authoritative knowledge or automatic deletion candidates.
Architecture-selection flags and provider availability must contract to typed operational capability health; the feature-flag ledger owns individual flag disposition.
Authentication and credential metadata are retained native primitives; recovery inventories metadata only and never promotes credentials into knowledge.
Issues have a direct UI and MCP consumer and retain native lifecycle semantics; no automatic conversion to knowledge is authorized.
Documents and collections retain their content-addressed/versioned contract and are not implicit beliefs.
Loom has its own task store and daemon MCP tools; it is outside the memory-core rewrite but needs project-identity compatibility evidence.
Daemon index liveness and server chunk search are split by design; retain their native contract and resolve project identity consistently.
Recovery migration needs redacted exports, audit receipts, and rollback support; existing governance code is an input, not authorization for destructive migration.
The daemon bridge streams and reconciles project removal using local connected-project state; its V2 project identifiers require migration-safe replacement.
MCP exposes consolidated and conditional tools over stdin/stdout, with current tools spanning core memory, candidate, projection, and adjacent domains.
The daemon dynamically fetches the server tool catalogue through gRPC; it is a live non-UI consumer and must not be removed from a UI-only scan.

The installed hook package dispatches SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStop, PreToolUse, PreCompact, Stop, and SessionEnd events; recovery preserves a versioned client contract rather than a best-effort hidden path.
OpenClaw currently calls legacy backfill and outcome URLs that are not registered by the server; keep as a versioned temporary adapter until supported durable intake replaces them.
